text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Foreign Body Aspiration (likely alcohol) leading to airway obstruction and subsequent chest pain.

The patient's history of forceful vomiting followed by choking and an inability to communicate effectively is highly concerning for an aspirated object blocking the airway. I need to immediately assess the airway patency and consider imaging if the patient can be stabilized. Please ensure the patient is positioned to maintain airway openness while we evaluate for obstruction.
